a.picturePrompt: Which story about Noah do the wooden beams suggest?

bonuses.prompt: What material was Noah told to use to build the ark?
options: Stone
Wood
Clay
bonuses.explanation: Noah was told to build the ark from a wood called gopher wood.

bonuses.prompt: What did Noah spread on the wood to keep water out?
options: A waterproof coating
Water
Sand
bonuses.explanation: Noah covered the wood with material that kept the water outside.

lessons.prompt: What had to happen before the animals could board?
options: The dove flew off
Noah built them a place
The rain stopped
A rainbow appeared
lessons.explanation: First the ark was built. Then the animals could go inside.

lessons.prompt: Why was so much room needed in the ark?
options: For a big olive tree
For houses from town
For the family and animals
For a little lake
lessons.explanation: Many animals and a whole family needed to fit inside.

b.picturePrompt: Which job is Noah doing with the tools and the wooden beams?

bonuses.prompt: The plans call for a bottom deck and two more above it. How many decks will Noah build?
options: Two
Three
Four
bonuses.explanation: One deck below and two above make three.

bonuses.prompt: What does “lower deck” mean in the list of levels?
options: The bottom floor
The sloping roof
The side door
bonuses.explanation: The instructions name the levels from the bottom upward.

lessons.prompt: Pitch is a substance that keeps water out. What job does it do on the ark?
options: Seals the sides
Divides the rooms
Raises the roof
Connects the decks
lessons.explanation: Noah coats the ark with pitch inside and out.

lessons.prompt: How do rooms and decks serve the same purpose?
options: They tell when rain will begin
They identify the ark’s builder
They measure the depth of a river
They give many creatures space in one shelter
lessons.explanation: The divisions make separate spaces inside a shared shelter.

teen.picturePrompt: What task from Genesis 6 is suggested by the timber on dry land?

bonuses.prompt: Which instruction tells Noah to work on both faces of the wooden walls?
options: Build rooms inside the ark
Coat the ark inside and out
Set the entrance in the side
bonuses.explanation: The coating is the one part of the job that the instructions place on both sides.

bonuses.prompt: The ark is to be 300 cubits long and 50 wide. Which sketch best fits those instructions?
options: A long, narrow rectangle seen from above
A square seen from above
A rectangle wider than it is long
bonuses.explanation: The length is six times the width, so the measurements rule out a square outline.

lessons.prompt: The ark has rooms as well as a waterproof coating. Which problem do the rooms solve?
options: Organizing space for the ark’s different occupants
Keeping water from seeping through the outer walls
Measuring the depth of the water outside
Steering the ark toward the mountains
lessons.explanation: The coating seals the wood. Dividing the inside into rooms makes the space usable for many occupants.

lessons.prompt: How does the story show Noah’s response to the long list of building instructions?
options: It quotes Noah accepting each instruction
It lists the changes Noah made to the plans
It gives Noah’s own account of the work
It reports that he carried them out
lessons.explanation: God’s directions take up several verses. A single sentence about Noah’s actions answers them.

c.picturePrompt: Which episode in Genesis 6 do the building materials suggest?

bonuses.prompt: Where do the building directions in Genesis 6 place the entrance?
options: In the top covering
In the side
In the hull floor
bonuses.explanation: Genesis 6:16 puts the entrance in the side alongside the instructions for the decks.

bonuses.prompt: Which feature is assigned a numerical measurement?
options: The ark’s width
The thickness of the pitch
The door’s width
bonuses.explanation: Genesis 6:15 gives the ark’s length, width and height.

lessons.prompt: Which of these four details about construction is left open in Genesis 6?
options: Number of decks
Years spent building
Length in cubits
Width in cubits
lessons.explanation: The instructions are detailed, but the chapter does not state how long the construction took.

lessons.prompt: What contrast emerges between the judgment on “all flesh” and the instructions for boarding the animals?
options: The judgment falls on humans, leaving animals outside the ark safe from the start
The animals are assured survival, while the family’s rescue is deferred until after the flood
The judgment encompasses living beings, yet representatives survive to continue life
Animal survival depends on ritual cleanness, whereas human survival depends on righteousness
lessons.explanation: Genesis 6:13 and 6:17 describe sweeping destruction. Verses 18–20 make provision for Noah, his household and living representatives of each kind.

a.picturePrompt: Baskets and sacks are full before the rain comes. What job is Noah getting done?

bonuses.prompt: What is Noah gathering for the ark?
options: Jewels
Musical instruments
Food
bonuses.explanation: Noah gathers food for those who will be aboard.

bonuses.prompt: The bins are full. Who will share this food when the ark is closed?
options: Only the people carrying baskets
The family and the animals
Only the animals that eat grain
bonuses.explanation: Noah gathered food for everyone who would be aboard.

lessons.prompt: When did Noah gather the food?
options: After the rainbow
Before the flood
When the dove returned
When the animals left
lessons.explanation: The food was ready by the time the flood came.

lessons.prompt: Why did Noah take food into the ark?
options: To feed everyone
To grow a rooftop garden
To fill a toy basket
To decorate the door
lessons.explanation: The family and animals still need to eat while they are aboard.

b.picturePrompt: Noah has baskets to fill before the rain. What part of the story is this?

bonuses.prompt: Which job can Noah do before anyone boards?
options: Send a bird to see if the water has gone down
Let the animals out onto dry land
Set aside food for the journey
bonuses.explanation: Noah has to gather the food while it is still available on land.

bonuses.prompt: The verse calls the food both “for you” and “for them.” Why would one small family basket be too little?
options: The stores are meant only for Noah’s three sons
The same stores must feed people and animals
Each family member must leave a basket outside
bonuses.explanation: The gathered supply is intended for Noah’s household and the creatures aboard.

lessons.prompt: Noah hears that the food will be for him and “them.” Who are “they” in the directions for boarding the animals?
options: The neighbours outside
Only the birds that will fly away
The creatures coming aboard
People in future generations
lessons.explanation: The preceding verses describe the creatures Noah is to take with him.

lessons.prompt: The instruction is to gather food for Noah and the animals. What did the artist add by painting a basket?
options: The act of gathering food
The container used for gathering
The identity of the man gathering it
The need to feed the animals
lessons.explanation: The verse names the food and those it will feed. It leaves the container to the imagination.

teen.picturePrompt: Which of Noah’s preparations for a long stay aboard do these baskets suggest?

bonuses.prompt: In Genesis 6:21, who is given a task and who is meant to benefit from it?
options: Each creature gathers provisions for Noah
Noah gathers food for the builders alone
Noah gathers provisions for himself and the creatures
bonuses.explanation: The command addresses Noah and then names both him and the creatures as those who will eat.

bonuses.prompt: What does gathering the food add to the instruction to take food?
options: Noah must eat the supplies before boarding
Noah must bring supplies together before they are needed
Noah must grow new crops inside the ark
bonuses.explanation: Taking food and gathering it point to a supply that can be used during the stay aboard.

lessons.prompt: Maya suggests a caption saying that Noah stored one sack per animal. Which part of her idea does the passage support?
options: An equal ration went to every animal
Noah counted out a sack for each animal
Noah had to provide food for the animals
All the food was stored in sacks
lessons.explanation: The recipients are named. The passage gives neither container sizes nor rations.

lessons.prompt: Why do the food instructions belong with the instructions to shelter the animals?
options: Both specify the order in which the animals must enter
Both look beyond boarding to keeping the occupants alive
Both set a date for taking the animals out again
Both list the animals that can supply food
lessons.explanation: Building gives the animals a place on the water. Gathering food gives them a way to survive there.

c.picturePrompt: Which instruction to Noah in Genesis 6 takes shape here?

bonuses.prompt: What is Noah told to gather in the final instruction before Genesis 6 sums up his response?
options: Seven pairs of clean animals
Offerings from the clean animals
Food of every edible kind
bonuses.explanation: The food instruction closes the preparations in 6:21. The animal counts and the offerings belong to other stages.

bonuses.prompt: Which detail about the provisions is specified in verse 21?
options: How much each species will receive
Who will feed on it
How long it will feed the whole family
bonuses.explanation: The verse identifies the beneficiaries without specifying quantities or a rationing period.

lessons.prompt: In “for you and for them,” what supports identifying “them” with the animals?
options: The naming of Noah’s sons in the introduction to his family
The count of clean animals given before boarding
The list of species immediately before the food instruction
The distinction between birds and livestock at the offering
lessons.explanation: Genesis 6:19–20 names the creatures coming to Noah. The pronoun connects them to the supplies.

lessons.prompt: What is the scope of “all that he was commanded” in the summary in 6:22?
options: The sequence of instructions leading up to the verse
Only the food gathering in the immediately preceding verse
Boarding the counts of animals specified in the next chapter
The departure and offering that will be narrated later
lessons.explanation: The commands are detailed, while Genesis 6:22 sums up Noah’s response to the whole charge.

a.picturePrompt: Hoofprints lead up to a wooden ramp. What are the animals about to do together?

bonuses.prompt: Who boarded with Noah’s family?
options: Neighbours from town
A group of fishers
The animals
bonuses.explanation: Noah’s family and many animals went inside.

bonuses.prompt: What needed to happen before the door could close?
options: The last animals had to get inside
The animals had to come out again
The family had to lead the animals down
bonuses.explanation: The open entrance lets all the animals come aboard before the door shuts.

lessons.prompt: What happened only after everyone had gone inside?
options: Noah started building
Noah received the building plans
God shut the ark
Noah prepared a place for the animals
lessons.explanation: God shut the ark once Noah and the animals were inside.

lessons.prompt: Noah packed food before boarding. Why do the animals need it?
options: They will stay inside for a long time
They are setting out on a walk
They are planting a new garden
They are going back to the forest today
lessons.explanation: The animals cannot search outside for food during the flood.

b.picturePrompt: Which part of Noah’s story do these animal tracks lead to?

bonuses.prompt: Noah and his wife, their three sons and the sons’ three wives boarded. How many people went in?
options: Six
Seven
Eight
bonuses.explanation: The parents make two people, and the three couples add six more.

bonuses.prompt: The animals walked in pairs. Which pair of events comes in the order the story gives?
options: The creatures enter, then the door is shut
The door is shut, then the sheep reach the entrance
The water lifts the ark, then Noah starts to build it
bonuses.explanation: The opening must stay clear while the animals are coming in. The closing ends the boarding scene.

lessons.prompt: Some animals came in several pairs. What would you see if you watched them come in two by two?
options: Only two animals could enter in total
All the birds would have to wait outside
Every kind would have exactly one pair
More than one pair of the same kind could pass the door
lessons.explanation: Two by two tells us how they came in. Some kinds had more pairs than others.

lessons.prompt: How does bringing pairs serve a purpose beyond the flood?
options: The rain will stop sooner
More animals can be born
The ark will need less food
The family can measure the water
lessons.explanation: The instructions connect boarding the animals with the continuation of life on land.

teen.picturePrompt: Which moment between the preparations and the rising water do the converging tracks suggest?

bonuses.prompt: Which order fits the animals on the open ramp and the closing of the ark in Genesis 7?
options: God shuts Noah in, then the sheep walk up to enter
Noah shuts the door before his household enters
The creatures enter, then God shuts Noah in
bonuses.explanation: The boarding account names the arrivals before its closing action, performed by God.

bonuses.prompt: The warning mentions both seven days and forty days. What do the seven days measure?
options: The time remaining before the rain begins
The time until the ark comes to rest
The length of the rainfall
bonuses.explanation: The seven days are advance notice. The forty days describe the rain to come.

lessons.prompt: Why does the instruction about the birds mention males, females and future offspring together?
options: Every bird is supposed to hatch aboard the ark
Only birds already raising young may enter
The young birds must go in before their parents
Keeping pairs alive makes future generations possible
lessons.explanation: The instruction looks beyond the survival of the birds that board to the life that will follow them.

lessons.prompt: In the plans Noah is told to bring the animals in. In the boarding scene they come to him. What does reading both scenes show?
options: Noah abandons his task as soon as the animals appear
Noah has a task, but the animals also take part in reaching shelter
The animals arrive before Noah receives any instructions
Two separate groups of animals board different arks
lessons.explanation: The earlier scene gives Noah responsibility. The later one lets the reader see the animals coming to him in pairs.

c.picturePrompt: Which step from preparation to action in Genesis 7 is pictured here?

bonuses.prompt: Who shuts Noah in at the close of the boarding account?
options: Noah
Shem
The LORD
bonuses.explanation: Genesis 7:16 attributes the closing to the LORD after the creatures enter.

bonuses.prompt: How can the phrase “two by two” about entry stand beside the earlier instruction about sevens?
options: The manner of entry and the numbers to be brought answer different questions
The manner of entry cancels the earlier distinction between kinds
The earlier numbers describe departure and the pairs describe arrival
bonuses.explanation: Walking in pairs does not require the same total number of individuals in every group.

lessons.prompt: In 7:8–9, what does “two by two” describe after the list of animal kinds?
options: The manner of entry, including kinds represented by several pairs
The total number taken from every kind that boarded
The number of pairs Noah must take from each kind
The manner of entry of the unclean animals alone
lessons.explanation: Entering in pairs does not remove the explicit distinctions in the numbers of pairs.

lessons.prompt: How does the reason given in 7:1 change the way readers learn of Noah’s righteousness compared with 6:9?
options: From God addressing Noah to the narrator assessing him
From the narrator’s assessment of Noah to an assessment of his entire household
From the narrator’s characterization to God addressing Noah
From a judgment on the whole generation to praise of Noah’s sons alone
lessons.explanation: Genesis 6:9 characterizes Noah as righteous. In 7:1 that judgment becomes a reason God gives him for boarding.

a.picturePrompt: Rain is striking the outside wall. Which part of Noah’s story makes a roof so important?

bonuses.prompt: First the ark stood on the ground. What did the growing flood do to it?
options: Left it resting on the same ground
Lifted it until it floated
Left it high above the water
bonuses.explanation: The rising water picked up the ark from below.

bonuses.prompt: While the waves are high, where can the family take care of the animals?
options: On the bank, where grass grows
On a hillside, beside the ark
Inside the ark, where they have food
bonuses.explanation: The ark carries both the animals and the food the family gathered.

lessons.prompt: What happened to the ark after the water rose?
options: It floated
It rested on a mountain
It fell apart
It stayed on dry ground
lessons.explanation: The ark had stood on the ground. The water lifted it.

lessons.prompt: Why did the family stay aboard even when the rain stopped?
options: Noah was still building the ark
The animals were still waiting outside
The family was waiting for snow
Water still covered the ground
lessons.explanation: The rain stopped before the ground dried.

b.picturePrompt: The wood is wet outside while the family needs shelter within. Which event put that shelter to the test?

bonuses.prompt: Forty days and nights describes the rain. Which event tells you what the rain helped cause?
options: The ark came to rest on the mountain
The waters rose and lifted the ark
The ground dried outside the door
bonuses.explanation: Rain joined the waters already bursting forth. The rising water lifted the ark above the land.

bonuses.prompt: What lifted the ark above the land?
options: A large cloud
Wooden wheels
The rising water
bonuses.explanation: The water rose, lifted the ark above the land, and carried it on the surface.

lessons.prompt: Which detail shows how high the floodwater reached?
options: The window was opened
The animals came in pairs
Even the high mountains were covered
The ark had three decks
lessons.explanation: Genesis 7 describes water covering even the mountains.

lessons.prompt: Leah marked day forty as the day the flood ended. What should she write there instead?
options: The rain has stopped, but the water is still high
The animals are leaving the ark
The ark has come to rest on Ararat
The dove is back with an olive leaf
lessons.explanation: The forty days measure the rainfall. The water remained high for a much longer time.

teen.picturePrompt: In which episode does the shelter built on dry land begin to float?

bonuses.prompt: Which detail places this scene later than the animals’ arrival at the doorway?
options: Noah has a family with him
The ark has lifted off the ground
The ark is made of wood
bonuses.explanation: The family and the wooden ark were already there at boarding. Only the rising water lifts the ark off the ground.

bonuses.prompt: The story next describes even the high mountains under water. What has changed in the description?
options: The speaker changes from Noah to his sons
The story turns from the present to Noah’s childhood
The view widens from the ark to the surrounding world
bonuses.explanation: First we follow what happens to one vessel. The mountains show the reach of the water beyond it.

lessons.prompt: An artist wants to draw animals sheltering on a dry peak at the height of the flood. Which detail in the passage challenges this idea?
options: The account measures the rain in days
Noah’s sons have names
The water covers even the high mountains
The ark has an entrance in its side
lessons.explanation: At the height of the flood the mountains themselves are covered. The refuge described in the account is the ark.

lessons.prompt: Why can the same rising water threaten life on land and help preserve the ark’s occupants?
options: It covers the land while carrying the ark on its surface
It leaves food on the mountains while filling the ark
It leaves the peaks dry while hiding the ark below them
It carries the ark ashore while washing away its supplies
lessons.explanation: The contrast depends on where the creatures are. The water submerges one habitat and lifts the floating shelter.

c.picturePrompt: Which event in Genesis 7 makes this wooden wall the boundary between life inside and water outside?

bonuses.prompt: Which statement compares the forty days with the one hundred and fifty without adding an interval to the account?
options: Both numbers date the same falling rain over different regions
One duration measures rainfall; the other measures prevailing waters
One duration measures rising waters; the other measures drying land
bonuses.explanation: Genesis 7 attaches the counts to different descriptions, rain and the waters prevailing.

bonuses.prompt: What is measured in cubits in the account of the mountains being covered, as distinct from the building plans?
options: The height of the ark’s side
The ark’s width
The height of the water’s rise
bonuses.explanation: Verse 20 uses cubits in its description of the rising waters and covered mountains.

lessons.prompt: In chapter 6 Noah made the ark. Which description best captures the roles in 7:17–18?
options: Noah sets the ark moving, and then the waters lift it
A wind moves the ark, and then the waters subside
The waters first subside, and then the ark comes to rest
The waters lift the ark, and then the ark moves on their surface
lessons.explanation: Noah acts in the building account. Here the rising waters supply the motion.

lessons.prompt: What closes the description of lost life in 7:23 and recalls the ark’s purpose in chapter 6?
options: Naming the family and the creatures as covenant partners
Identifying Noah and those with him as the survivors
Remembering Noah and the creatures in their shelter
Blessing the creatures leaving the shelter to multiply
lessons.explanation: Genesis 7:23 closes its account of loss by identifying the survivors, recalling the ark’s purpose in chapter 6.

a.picturePrompt: The wind stirs the cloth and the water looks calmer. What is beginning to happen to the water?

bonuses.prompt: The wind starts blowing over the water. What happens next in the story?
options: The water slowly goes down
All the ground dries at once
The water starts lifting the ark again
bonuses.explanation: The waters go down little by little after the wind begins to blow.

bonuses.prompt: Why does Noah keep the animals aboard after the rain stops?
options: He is still waiting for the rain to start
The ground still needs time to dry
The animals are only just boarding
bonuses.explanation: The rain can stop while the ground is still under water.

lessons.prompt: What happened first?
options: The land dried completely
The rain stopped
Noah left the ark
The animals ran on the land
lessons.explanation: The rain stopped first. The ground remained underwater for a while.

lessons.prompt: The water is falling. Why can’t the family walk outside yet?
options: The ark has yet to be built
Noah is still gathering food outside
Water still covers the ground
The animals have yet to board
lessons.explanation: The water falls slowly. The family still needs dry ground.

b.picturePrompt: The rain has stopped and a breeze stirs the cloth. What is happening to the floodwater?

bonuses.prompt: At this point the story names Noah and the creatures sharing his shelter. Who are those creatures?
options: The animals that had boarded the ark
Birds that had already left the ark
Animals that had found a dry mountain
bonuses.explanation: These are the animals that went into the ark before the water rose.

bonuses.prompt: The rain has stopped, but the waters are described as gradually receding. What follows from both details?
options: The family can step out as soon as the rain stops
The family must wait even after the sky clears
The ark only starts to float after the sky clears
bonuses.explanation: Stopping the downpour does not drain the flooded earth at once.

lessons.prompt: What explains why less water was being added to the flood?
options: The sources of water closed
The ark slid forward
Noah opened a window
The dove went out
lessons.explanation: The springs and the openings in the sky closed and the rain stopped.

lessons.prompt: During the flood the water lifted the ark. What now marks a change in the direction of the story?
options: Noah receives the ark’s measurements
Wind passes and the water begins to fall
The animals board in pairs
The first rain falls
lessons.explanation: Rising waters brought danger. Their retreat begins the return to dry land.

teen.picturePrompt: The wind catches a cloth beside the ark. Which turn in the flood story does it mark?

bonuses.prompt: What makes the mention of wind a turning point when compared with the rain in Genesis 7?
options: Rain accompanies rising water; wind accompanies its retreat
Rain ends the flooding; wind begins it again
Rain and wind both mark the moment of disembarking
bonuses.explanation: In chapter 7 the ark is lifted; after the wind passes in chapter 8 the waters subside.

bonuses.prompt: Why does the passage mention both springs in the deep and openings in the sky?
options: The springs closed first and the account measures the delay
Water had entered from below as well as from above
One of the two sources was still pouring water in
bonuses.explanation: Closing both sources answers the earlier description of water breaking in from two directions.

lessons.prompt: Which caption best matches the gradual fall described after the rain stops?
options: The storm has ended, and the water keeps draining away
The wind has blown all the water away in a day
The rain has stopped, so the animals step onto dry land
The water is falling, so Noah can see the olive leaf
lessons.explanation: The end of the rain cuts off a supply of water. It takes longer for the flooded land to reappear.

lessons.prompt: What changes for the reader when the story turns from the powerful waters to God remembering those aboard?
options: Noah takes over as the narrator for the rest of the flood
Attention returns to the survivors before they can see land
The animals receive instructions to open the ark
The entire covenant is announced while the rain still falls
lessons.explanation: The preceding scene ends with the waters holding sway. The new scene names Noah and the animals and begins the retreat of the water.

c.picturePrompt: Which turning point in Genesis 8 does the cloth blowing over the water suggest?

bonuses.prompt: Genesis 7 narrows survival to Noah and those with him. How does the opening of chapter 8 take up that group?
options: It names Noah and the animals with him as those God remembers
It names future descendants as those already released
It names the survivors only after the drying is complete
bonuses.explanation: The statement of remembrance recalls the survivors aboard just as the narrative changes direction.

bonuses.prompt: What is closed in 8:2 in reversal of what opened in 7:11?
options: The ark’s door and the window Noah made
The springs of the deep and the openings of the sky
The ark’s openings and the openings of the sky
bonuses.explanation: Genesis 7:11 and 8:2 describe the opening and closing of the same sources.

lessons.prompt: What immediate action gives expression to “remembered” in 8:1, before any command to leave?
options: Removing the ark’s covering to inspect the ground
Opening the window to test the state of the water
Sending a wind that begins the waters’ retreat
Sending the family out to examine the dry land
lessons.explanation: The wind follows the remembrance, and the retreat of the waters begins.

lessons.prompt: How does the function of the 150 days change between 7:24 and 8:3?
options: From a span of prevailing waters to the point at which their decrease is reported
From the duration of rainfall to the days remaining until the ark rests
From the household’s wait to the time required for the ground to dry
From the sighting of the peaks to the date the first bird is sent
lessons.explanation: Genesis 7:24 and 8:3 use the same span across the shift from prevailing waters to recession.

a.picturePrompt: Water surrounds a peak, but its top is showing. Which stop on the ark’s journey comes next?

bonuses.prompt: Which happened first: resting on the mountain or walking out of the ark?
options: The family walked out while the ark floated
The family stepped out before the ark touched rock
The ark rested while the family was still inside
bonuses.explanation: The family was still aboard when the ark came to rest on Ararat.

bonuses.prompt: The rock under the ark is dry. Why does the family still wait?
options: One dry rock does not make a dry path for everyone
The ark still has to float up onto the mountain
The animals have already walked down the mountain
bonuses.explanation: Water still covers the low ground. Coming to rest and being ready to leave happen at different times.

lessons.prompt: What began to show above the water after the ark settled?
options: A rainbow
Mountain tops
A full food basket
A leaf in the dove’s beak
lessons.explanation: As the water dropped farther, the highest parts of the mountains could be seen.

lessons.prompt: The peaks can be seen. Why are the animals still waiting?
options: Someone is still building their ark
They are waiting for the flood to start
Water remains around the mountains
They want the rain to return
lessons.explanation: Only the highest parts were showing. The land was not all dry.

b.picturePrompt: The peak is exposed, but water still fills the valleys. Which stop can the ark reach before the family can walk out?

bonuses.prompt: What had changed by the time the ark reached Ararat, and what had still to happen?
options: The family had left, but the ark still had to stop
The ground had dried, but rain still had to begin
The ark rested, but the ground still had to dry
bonuses.explanation: Coming to rest on high ground happened well before the family could walk out.

bonuses.prompt: After the ark came to rest and the water level kept dropping, what became visible?
options: The mountaintops
Palace rooftops
City gates
bonuses.explanation: The ark first came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Later, the mountaintops appeared as the water kept receding.

lessons.prompt: The ark came to rest in the seventh month. The peaks appeared in the tenth. Which happened first?
options: The ark stopped floating freely
All the mountain tops could be seen
Noah sent the dove with the leaf
The family walked out of the ark
lessons.explanation: The seventh month comes before the tenth. The ark was already resting as the water continued to fall.

lessons.prompt: The water once lifted the ark. What does the change from floating to resting tell us?
options: The family exchanged the ark for a boat
The water level changed and land supported the ark
The animals learned to steer
A second flood began
lessons.explanation: Rising water lifted the ark. Later it rested on mountains while the water continued to fall.

teen.picturePrompt: Exposed rock can support a vessel before the valleys are dry. Which stage in Genesis 8 does that distinction identify?

bonuses.prompt: What happens to the ark in the seventh month?
options: It lifts from the earth and begins to float
It empties as the animals go out onto dry land
It comes to rest on the mountains of Ararat
bonuses.explanation: The ark settles on the mountains in the seventh month. The water around it continues to fall.

bonuses.prompt: The ark rests in month seven; mountain peaks appear in month ten. Which reading preserves the order?
options: The ark can be held by one height before other peaks emerge
All peaks must already be visible when the ark first rests
The family leaves as soon as the first peak becomes visible
bonuses.explanation: The text gives these events different dates and places the family’s departure later still.

lessons.prompt: An artist draws Noah stepping out when the ark first touches Ararat. Which detail has been moved forward?
options: Noah’s departure, which comes after the land dries
The ark’s contact with the mountains
The arrival of floodwater around the ark
The construction of the wooden ark
lessons.explanation: The ark settling is an early stage in the retreat of the water. The command to leave comes later.

lessons.prompt: The ark rests in month seven. Only in month ten does the narrator say the peaks could be seen. Which conclusion do these dates allow?
options: The family saw every peak before the ark stopped
The ark could be supported before the peaks were visible
The ark came to rest at the very highest peak
The water vanished as soon as the ark touched bottom
lessons.explanation: The dates distinguish what happened to the hull from what could be seen above the water. They do not identify a particular peak.

c.picturePrompt: Which dated event in Genesis 8 does an exposed height help distinguish from the later appearance of other peaks?

bonuses.prompt: What do the two chronological notices in Genesis 8:4–5 allow us to order without identifying a modern summit?
options: The opening of the window precedes the ark’s rest
The first sight of mountain peaks follows the departure
Rest in month seven precedes visible peaks in month ten
bonuses.explanation: The passage supplies the order and dates of rest and visibility without naming a unique peak.

bonuses.prompt: What can be established from the geographical expression “mountains of Ararat” alone?
options: The mountainous region where the ark rested
The particular peak in that region where it rested
The direction it drifted through that region
bonuses.explanation: The wording does not identify a particular modern peak.

lessons.prompt: What directly establishes that the ark’s rest and the exposure of the mountain tops were separate stages?
options: A different depth is measured for each event
A different bird is released after each event
A different month and day are given for each event
Noah removes the covering after each event
lessons.explanation: The seventh month marks the ark’s rest and the tenth the appearance of the mountain tops.

lessons.prompt: How does 8:5 return to the role of the mountains in the flood scene in 7:19?
options: The same landscape features show first the rise and then the fall of the waters
In both scenes the mountains date the resting of the ark precisely
In both scenes Noah uses the mountains to test the condition of the land
The mountains first measure elapsed time and then measure depth
lessons.explanation: The narrator uses the same feature of the landscape to show first the rise and then the retreat.

a.picturePrompt: A leaf lies by the window, far from a tree. Which part of Noah’s story explains how it got there?

bonuses.prompt: First the dove came back with nothing. What made her next visit more helpful to Noah?
options: She stayed away and never came back
She brought a leaf from a plant outside
She came back again with an empty beak
bonuses.explanation: Noah now had a clue about a plant outside the ark.

bonuses.prompt: Which came last after Noah sent the dove out several times?
options: The dove came back with nothing
The dove brought the leaf
The dove stayed outside
bonuses.explanation: She returned empty, then with a leaf. On her last flight she did not come back.

lessons.prompt: What happened before the dove came back with a leaf?
options: Noah left the ark
A rainbow appeared
Noah built an altar
It came back once without a leaf
lessons.explanation: On the first trip the dove found nowhere to rest. It brought a leaf on the next trip.

lessons.prompt: What did Noah learn from the leaf in the dove’s beak?
options: The rain was getting heavier
The water had fallen
The tree was inside the ark
The water had frozen
lessons.explanation: The leaf came from an olive tree. Noah understood that the dove could reach it.

b.picturePrompt: What event connects two clues here: a leaf from a living tree and a window that opens over floodwater?

bonuses.prompt: Two of the dove’s flights ended back at the ark. How could Noah tell the second return from the first?
options: Only on the first return did she carry a leaf
Only on the second return did she carry a leaf
On the second flight she stayed away
bonuses.explanation: The first return meant she found no resting place. The leaf on her next return supplied a new clue.

bonuses.prompt: Why did Noah send the dove again even after she brought an olive leaf?
options: Bringing a leaf meant she had found no plants at all
Noah needed her to bring back the raven
One branch within reach did not show that the ground was ready
bonuses.explanation: He waited another seven days. This time she did not come back to him.

lessons.prompt: Water covered the ground and the dove returned to Noah. What difficulty explains its return?
options: The window was closed to it
It found no place to land
It wanted to bring the raven
It dropped a leaf from its beak
lessons.explanation: On its first flight the dove could find no resting place.

lessons.prompt: The dove returned empty-beaked, came back with a leaf, then did not return. What does the sequence suggest?
options: Noah sent a different bird each time
The water rose continuously
Conditions outside changed between flights
All the land was dry on the first flight
lessons.explanation: The changing outcomes give Noah successive signs that the waters are receding.

teen.picturePrompt: Read the leaf as evidence rather than scenery. Which episode explains both what Noah knows now and why he still waits?

bonuses.prompt: Across the dove’s first two flights, what stays the same and what changes?
options: Both bring leaves; only the first ends in a return
Both end in a return; only the second brings a leaf
Both end outside; only the second lasts seven days
bonuses.explanation: The repeated return allows the new object in the second account to carry the news.

bonuses.prompt: Which interpretation fits both the second return and Noah’s decision to wait another week?
options: The water had vanished, and a new flood was expected
The leaf gave no information, so Noah began testing anew
The water had diminished, but the test was not complete
bonuses.explanation: Noah understands from the leaf that the waters have receded, then sends the dove once more.

lessons.prompt: Why does Noah’s week of waiting matter when comparing two flights of the dove?
options: It tells us how long the dove spent in the air
The water has time to fall between the two observations
It tells us when Noah received permission to leave
It dates the day the ark touched the mountains
lessons.explanation: Sending the same bird again after an interval lets the reader compare what has changed outside.

lessons.prompt: On its last flight the dove does not return. Which claim goes further than the account itself?
options: Noah sent the dove out more than once
Earlier the dove came back with a leaf
We know the exact spot where the dove settled
Noah waited between the last two flights
lessons.explanation: The narrator records the bird’s absence from the ark. The reader is not told where it went to live.

c.picturePrompt: Which episode makes a leaf at an opening evidence for Noah’s knowledge, while still withholding permission to depart?

bonuses.prompt: Read the report of the leaf alongside “Noah knew that the waters had diminished.” What is the direction of inference?
options: An order to leave supplies the leaf with its meaning in advance
A particular object carried back supports a conclusion about the water
A measured water level identifies the exact source of the leaf
bonuses.explanation: An observation of the dove is followed by a statement about Noah’s knowledge. The order to leave comes later.

bonuses.prompt: How does the raven’s movement differ from the dove’s missions in Genesis 8?
options: Both are sent afresh every seven days, but only the dove brings a leaf
Noah waits for the raven to return empty-beaked before he sends the dove
The raven ranges back and forth, while Noah repeatedly sends out the dove
bonuses.explanation: The raven’s movement is described as recurring. The dove’s separate missions receive individual outcomes.

lessons.prompt: On seeing the leaf, what conclusion does verse 11 attribute to Noah?
options: All the ground was already dry
The command to leave had already come
The floodwater had receded from the land
The dove would never return again
lessons.explanation: Noah draws a conclusion about the water level. Drying and the command to leave appear later.

lessons.prompt: How does the perspective shift between the account of the ark resting on the mountains and the story of Noah sending the dove?
options: From the narrator’s account of the land to Noah investigating through a sign
From Noah’s own visual inspection to the narrator dating the drying of the ground
From a divine disclosure to Noah to a conclusion given to the reader alone
From Noah’s guess about the mountains to confirmation addressed to him by God
lessons.explanation: Genesis 8:4–5 reports conditions. Verses 8–11 foreground what Noah seeks to know and what he learns.

a.picturePrompt: Earlier a wet world kept everyone inside. The door is open onto dry ground now. What part of Noah’s story is this?

bonuses.prompt: The dove could stay outside before the sheep could leave. What did the sheep still need?
options: Dry land to walk on
A branch to perch on
A breeze to fly with
bonuses.explanation: A dove flies. A sheep needs a place to set down its feet.

bonuses.prompt: Which little story tells what happened in the right order?
options: The animals went out, then the ark began floating
The land dried, then the family led the animals out
The family went out, then the animals first boarded
bonuses.explanation: Noah waited for the land to dry and for God’s call to come out with the animals.

lessons.prompt: When did Noah leave the ark?
options: When God told him to leave
As soon as the dove returned
When the rain began
Before all the animals entered
lessons.explanation: Noah waited and left after the command.

lessons.prompt: Why bring out the animals Noah once took aboard?
options: So they can build their own ark
So they can live on the land again
So they can look for another flood
So they can guard the roof
lessons.explanation: The ark protected them during the flood. Now there is room for them on land again.

b.picturePrompt: Compare this view through the door with the earlier animal tracks leading in. Which episode would reverse their direction?

bonuses.prompt: What could Noah do on dry land that the story places immediately after everyone left?
options: Build an altar and bring an offering
Look out from the ark and send the dove
Store enough food for the journey
bonuses.explanation: The altar comes after the departure. The other two actions belong to earlier stages of the journey.

bonuses.prompt: The animals entered in pairs and left “by their families.” Which retelling keeps both descriptions in place?
options: Groups of one family entered, only one pair came out
Pairs at entry, groups of their own kind at departure
Only birds came in pairs, only sheep came out in groups
bonuses.explanation: The story changes the wording when it describes the animals’ way out.

lessons.prompt: Why were the animals to be brought out?
options: To build another ark
To stay beside the door forever
To multiply on the earth again
To teach them to row
lessons.explanation: The instruction looks toward renewed animal life on earth.

lessons.prompt: The olive leaf showed that the water had gone down. When did the family finally leave?
options: When the land was dry and God told Noah to go out
As soon as the ark touched the mountains
On the day the rain stopped
Before the dove’s first flight
lessons.explanation: The leaf was an early sign. Noah and his family left later, when they could live on the land again.

teen.picturePrompt: Earlier the doorway marked entry into safety. The dry ground beyond it now gives a different command its setting. Which episode is this?

bonuses.prompt: Which pair separates a conclusion Noah can draw from something he receives as an instruction?
options: He sees dry ground; he is told to leave with the creatures
He sees the dove return; he is told the water has risen
He sees the ark on rock; he is told to board for the first time
bonuses.explanation: The ground’s appearance is observable. The call to leave is spoken to him after the drying.

bonuses.prompt: In which pair does the first action happen aboard and the second on dry land after the flood?
options: Building the ark and gathering provisions
Hearing the command to leave and building an altar
Sending out the raven and sending out the dove
bonuses.explanation: Noah hears the command aboard. The family and animals leave, and only then does he build the altar.

lessons.prompt: Why does the command name birds, livestock and creatures that move along the ground?
options: To specify the exact order for unloading the animals
To list only the animals Noah must later offer
To make clear that the departure includes every kind aboard
To decide which animals must stay inside
lessons.explanation: The list follows the command to bring out the living creatures and shows how widely it applies.

lessons.prompt: How does the reason for going out change the meaning of the earlier boarding scene?
options: The shelter protected creatures so that life on land could begin again
The shelter was always meant to be the animals’ permanent home
Only animals needed for the altar had reason to board
The family boarded to learn the route to a particular mountain
lessons.explanation: Boarding kept creatures alive during the flood. The call to go out and multiply gives that rescue a future on land.

c.picturePrompt: After signs gathered through a window, an open doorway frames dry land. Which episode turns observation into a commanded action?

bonuses.prompt: What does the earlier distinction between clean animals and others help a reader understand after the departure?
options: Why that classification reappears when the offerings are described
Why only pure animals were included in the command to leave
Why the covenant later names only birds fit for an offering
bonuses.explanation: All creatures leave. The description then singles out clean animals and birds for the offerings.

bonuses.prompt: What follows the creatures’ exit without an explicit command in this passage?
options: Bringing out the creatures
Building the altar
The departure of the family
bonuses.explanation: Genesis 8:16–19 ties departure to a command. The altar follows as Noah’s act.

lessons.prompt: What in the departure instruction of 8:17 echoes the blessing of fish and birds in Genesis 1:22?
options: The appointment of humankind to rule over the animals
The call for living creatures to multiply on the land
The grant of plants as food for the animals
The separation of waters so dry land can appear
lessons.explanation: The language of multiplication returns as life on land begins again.

lessons.prompt: What connects the distinction among animals at boarding in chapter 7 with the altar episode in chapter 8?
options: Pairing determines both the order of boarding and the number of offerings
Family grouping determines both boarding counts and the order of sacrifice
Cleanness determines counts among livestock at boarding and the choice of kinds for offering
The distinction between bird and beast determines both boarding order and the kind of altar
lessons.explanation: The distinction of cleanness in the preparations becomes relevant to the kinds Noah offers.

a.picturePrompt: The grass is wet, but sunlight reaches the ground again. Which story about a promise comes after the flood?

bonuses.prompt: A lamb is born after Noah has left the ark. Does the promise include it?
options: Only if that lamb once rode in the ark
Only if the lamb sees Noah point
Yes, it is for the animals that come after them too
bonuses.explanation: The promise is for living creatures for generations, even ones not aboard the ark.

bonuses.prompt: It rains again one day. Which words would help a worried child remember the promise?
options: Rain can fall without a flood covering the whole world
There will never be another rain cloud
Each rain means everyone must board again
bonuses.explanation: The promise was about a flood that destroys all living things. Rain can still come.

lessons.prompt: Which of these happened first?
options: Noah left the ark
The dove brought a leaf
Noah built an altar
God gave the rainbow as a sign
lessons.explanation: The dove brought the leaf while Noah was still aboard.

lessons.prompt: Why is the promise good for the animals too?
options: It protects them from another flood like this
It gives them another ark
It promises them only sunshine
It brings back their food basket
lessons.explanation: God promised that living creatures would not face another flood like this one.

b.picturePrompt: What event connects the water still on the grass with the promise about what will happen after this flood?

bonuses.prompt: Think of a child born long after the ark landed. Why is the promise important to that child too?
options: Only people who saw the ark can receive it
Every new child must start building an ark
The promise includes future generations
bonuses.explanation: God includes Noah’s descendants in the promise, along with the living creatures.

bonuses.prompt: A child says, “If the promise holds, there should never be a storm.” Which detail would you use to answer?
options: The promise concerns a flood destroying all life, and the sign appears in clouds
The promise says rain will fall only beside the ark
The promise ends with the first cloud after the flood
bonuses.explanation: Rain clouds are part of the description of the sign itself. A storm is not the destruction promised against.

lessons.prompt: What does the covenant promise?
options: No flood will again destroy the earth in this way
Rain will never fall again
There will never be clouds
Everyone will live in an ark
lessons.explanation: The promise concerns a flood that destroys the earth, not an end to rainfall.

lessons.prompt: How does the dove’s olive leaf differ from the rainbow?
options: Both instructed Noah to leave
Both reached Noah while he was building
The leaf told of the water level; the rainbow marks a promise about the future
The leaf announced rain and the rainbow ordered construction
lessons.explanation: From the leaf Noah learned the waters had fallen. The rainbow marks a covenant with living creatures.

teen.picturePrompt: Which episode interprets the clearing sky in terms of future generations, beyond what Noah’s family can see?

bonuses.prompt: A reader says only those who saw the flood could share the covenant. Which two groups in Genesis 9 challenge that reading?
options: Noah and the sons standing beside him
The family aboard and the creatures aboard at the time
Future descendants and living creatures across generations
bonuses.explanation: The address begins with the survivors but extends to descendants and living creatures in generations to come.

bonuses.prompt: Can another rain cloud appear without breaking the covenant? What supports your answer?
options: Yes. The bow itself is to appear in clouds
No. All clouds disappear after the promise
Only while Noah’s sons are still alive
bonuses.explanation: The promise concerns a flood that destroys life on earth. The account still speaks of clouds gathering.

lessons.prompt: Why is a caption saying “Noah promises to protect the earth” misleading here?
options: God makes the promise to Noah and to living creatures
Noah makes the promise to his sons alone
The animals make the promise to Noah
Noah makes the promise before seeing any water
lessons.explanation: Noah receives the covenant. The speaker establishing it and giving it a sign is God.

lessons.prompt: Early on, Noah gathers food for those about to board. How does the covenant enlarge the reach of that concern?
options: It promises that all Noah’s descendants will receive the same food
It makes each future generation build another ark
It extends from the ark’s occupants to living creatures across generations
It reserves the promise for the animals Noah fed himself
lessons.explanation: The provisions were for one household and its animals during one flood. The covenant also names their descendants and all living creatures.

c.picturePrompt: The earth still bears traces of water. Which covenant marks a limit on future destruction while leaving room for cloud and rain?

bonuses.prompt: Compare “God remembered Noah” in 8:1 with the remembrance in 9:16. Which reading distinguishes the objects and times of remembrance?
options: In both passages Noah remembers the creatures after seeing the bow
The first concerns a future covenant, the second a single rescue already completed
God remembers the living in the flood, then speaks of remembering the covenant when seeing the bow
bonuses.explanation: The first remembrance introduces the waters’ retreat. The later one concerns an everlasting covenant with living creatures.

bonuses.prompt: How does the covenant speech in chapter 9 develop what God says in his heart after the offering in chapter 8?
options: An inward resolve is spoken to named recipients and given a sign
A sign already given after the offering is withdrawn from the creatures
Noah’s promise at the altar becomes a duty he imposes on his descendants
bonuses.explanation: Chapter 8 describes an inward divine resolve. In chapter 9 God addresses Noah and his sons, includes living creatures and names the bow as the sign.

lessons.prompt: In chapter 9, who is explicitly included beyond the personal address to Noah in chapter 6?
options: His household and the clean animals that left the ark
His descendants and the birds released before departure
His sons and the animals offered on the altar
His descendants and every living creature
lessons.explanation: Genesis 6:18 addresses Noah personally. Genesis 9:9–10 spells out the reach across generations and species.

lessons.prompt: What changes between the remembrance opening chapter 8 and the remembrance tied to the bow in chapter 9?
options: From a promise to future generations to an explanation of how the occupants survived
From rescue of the ark’s occupants to an enduring commitment to all life
From Noah recalling his instruction to his sons commemorating the altar
From remembrance of a household covenant to renewal for that household alone
lessons.explanation: In 8:1 remembrance leads into the waters’ retreat. In 9:15–16 it is bound to an ongoing commitment to living creatures.
